newsitem.title: USA: Exide's lead smelter being run by management.
newsitem.headline: Exide's lead smelter being run by management.

text.p: Exide Corp's strike-hit 90,000 short tons per year secondary lead smelter in Reading, Pa. is being operated by bosses as workers remain off the job, a company spokeswoman said.
"It's being run right now by management," the spokeswoman said.
She was unable to confirm that the smelter was actually shut for a while after workers walked off midnight Sunday, or if the plant was operating at full capacity.
The United Steelworkers of America union, whose recommendation of accepting a tentative pay deal was rebuffed by employees in a vote, will meet Exide management Friday.
Exide uses the smelter to remelt lead from spent car batteries to use in new batteries.
The U.S. lead market was barely stirred from its seasonal lull by news of Exide's labor troubles.

"We are just hoping for plenty of hot weather this summer," a dealer said. Hot weather is an effective killer of batteries, necessating replacement. The winter battery season in the U.S. was a disappointment.
Rival producers were equally unperturbed and more concerned about Mexico's growing appetite for spent U.S. car batteries.

Demand from south of the border was partly responsible for the price of old batteries rising to 8 cents per pound and above in recent weeks as supplies tighten because of Mexican demand, one producer official said.

"The Mexicans have really run the price up. They have not backed off and they are very formidable competition," the producer official added. Leading U.S. lead recyclers are now looking into what can be done to dampen Mexico's appetite.
